content.value_statement: PDF work often requires several tools for text, tables, forms, and page management. This skill provides focused Python examples for common PDF processing tasks.
actual_capabilities: Extract text from a selected PDF page with pdfplumber.
Extract tables from PDF pages and iterate through their rows.
Read all pages and combine their extracted text.
Fill PDF form fields and write a completed form.
Merge multiple PDFs or split selected pages into a new PDF.
Export extracted text to TXT and tables to CSV files.
limitations: Scanned PDFs may need OCR tools that are only listed, not configured.
Table extraction quality depends on the PDF layout and source quality.
Form examples require PDFs with compatible fillable fields.
The skill does not install Python packages or validate library versions.

use_cases.title: Extract a report summary
use_cases.description: Extract text from a report and save the relevant pages for review.

use_cases.title: Prepare completed forms
use_cases.description: Fill known form fields, validate required values, and create a flattened PDF for distribution.

use_cases.title: Prepare data from PDF tables
use_cases.description: Extract report tables and export them to CSV for spreadsheet analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Extract first-page text
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the text from the first page of document.pdf using the recommended library. Explain how to run the example.

prompt_templates.title: Export a PDF table
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract tables from tables.pdf and save them to output.csv. Include checks for pages with no tables.

prompt_templates.title: Merge monthly reports
prompt_templates.prompt: Merge January.pdf, February.pdf, and March.pdf into merged.pdf. Preserve the source files.

prompt_templates.title: Fill and validate a form
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect form.pdf fields, validate my required values, fill the form, and save a separate flattened copy. Report validation errors before writing output.

output_examples.input: Extract text from the first page of a PDF report.
output: The extracted first-page text printed for review.
A note when the page has no extractable text.

output_examples.input: Merge three PDF files into one document.
output: A merged.pdf file created from the listed source files.
A reminder to close the merger after writing.

output_examples.input: Fill a PDF form with contact details.
output: A field-validation step for required values.
A completed PDF written as a separate output file.
An optional flattened copy for distribution.

best_practices: Keep original PDFs unchanged and write results to separate files.
Validate required form values before filling or flattening a document.
Test extraction and table detection on a small representative PDF first.
anti_patterns: Do not assume scanned PDFs contain extractable text without OCR.
Do not overwrite source PDFs when creating merged, split, or filled outputs.
Do not rely on table extraction without reviewing the exported rows.

faq.question: Which libraries does this skill use?
faq.answer: Examples use pdfplumber for extraction and pypdf for merging, splitting, and form work.

faq.question: Can it extract tables from every PDF?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on the document structure and table layout.

faq.question: Can it read scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Scanned PDFs usually require OCR. The skill lists pytesseract as an option but does not provide OCR setup steps.

faq.question: Does it preserve the original PDF?
faq.answer: The examples write separate output files. You should keep originals and avoid overwriting them.

faq.question: Can it fill any PDF form?
faq.answer: It works with compatible fillable fields. Field names and library support must be checked for each form.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. Install the required Python packages in your own environment before running the examples.
